Com 200–230 obtém-se o certificado C2 (grau A, B ou C); com 180–199, um certificado de nível C1. Writing e Speaking são avaliados em escalas de 0 a 5, em que a banda 3 corresponde ao C2, a banda 1 ao C1 e a banda 5 vai além dos descritores C2. Cada tarefa tem uma estratégia própria.
pontos: Reading and Use of English: Parts 1, 5, 6 e 7 contam para Reading; Parts 2, 3 e 4 para Use of English. Plano possível: 35 min para as Parts 1–4, 18 para a Part 5, 18 para a Part 6, 15 para a Part 7.
Part 2 (open cloze): uma palavra por lacuna, sem contrações. Part 3: uma palavra mal escrita não pontua.
Part 4: 3–8 palavras incluindo a palavra dada, que não se altera; contrações contam como duas palavras; cada item tem duas metades (nunca deixar em branco).
Parts 4–6 valem 2 pontos por item; na Part 6 há oito opções para sete lacunas e uma fica de fora.
Writing: cerca de 45 minutos por parte (10 planear, 30 escrever, 5 rever); Part 1 obrigatória (240–280), Part 2 à escolha (280–320).
Listening: cada gravação ouve-se duas vezes; Part 2 com palavras realmente ouvidas, bem escritas; Part 4 com cinco monólogos e duas tarefas.
Speaking: cada candidato é avaliado pelo seu desempenho, não em comparação com o parceiro; o silêncio é a única forma de não pontuar.
licao.exemplo: Estratégia da Part 1 (p. 229): testar cada opção na expressão completa, não só na lacuna (give rise to, não apenas give rise) e eliminar opções próximas no sentido mas erradas na colocação ou na gramática.

itens.enunciado: How many items does the Reading and Use of English paper have?
itens.explicacao: 53 itens, 72 pontos, em 1 h 30.
porque: 40 não é o número de itens desta prova.
30 não é o número de itens desta prova.
Certo: 53 itens.
72 é a pontuação máxima, não o número de itens.

itens.enunciado: Which parts of Reading and Use of English count towards the Use of English score?
itens.explicacao: Parts 2, 3 e 4 contam para Use of English; Parts 1, 5, 6 e 7 para Reading.
porque: Parts 1, 5, 6 e 7 contam para Reading.
Part 1 conta para Reading, não Use of English.
Parts 5 e 6 contam para Reading.
Certo: Parts 2, 3 e 4.

itens.enunciado: Which overall score range gives the Certificate of Proficiency in English at Level C2?
itens.explicacao: 200–230 dá o grau A, B ou C no nível C2; 180–199 dá certificado de nível C1.
porque: 180–199 dá certificado de nível C1.
Acima de 230 não é o intervalo do certificado C2.
160–179 fica abaixo do intervalo C2.
Certo: 200–230 dá o certificado C2.

itens.enunciado: On the Writing and Speaking scales, which band corresponds to the C2 descriptors?
itens.explicacao: Banda 3 = C2; banda 1 = C1; banda 5 vai além dos descritores C2.
porque: Certo: banda 3 = C2.
Banda 5 vai além dos descritores C2.
Banda 4 fica entre a banda 3 (C2) e a 5; não é a que corresponde aos descritores C2.
Banda 1 corresponde a C1.

itens.enunciado: In Part 2 (open cloze), contractions are accepted as one word.
itens.explicacao: As contrações não são aceites na Part 2; na Part 4 contam como duas palavras.

itens.enunciado: In Part 4, you should never leave a blank, because one correct half of the answer earns one mark.
itens.explicacao: Cada item da Part 4 é avaliado em duas metades.

itens.enunciado: In Speaking, each candidate is assessed on his or her own performance, not in comparison with the partner.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. Cada candidato é avaliado pelo seu próprio desempenho ao longo da prova, e não em comparação com o parceiro.

itens.enunciado: In Listening Part 2 (sentence completion), what kind of answers are expected?
opcoes: One of three options for each question
The exact words heard, correctly spelled
Paraphrases of what is heard, in your own words
A letter A–H for each of the five speakers
itens.explicacao: As respostas são palavras realmente ouvidas, que devem encaixar na frase e estar bem escritas.
porque: Escolher entre três opções é outro formato.
Certo: palavras ouvidas (geralmente uma a três), bem escritas e que encaixam gramaticalmente na frase.
Na Part 2 escrevem-se palavras ouvidas, não paráfrases.
Letras A–H por falante é o formato de multiple matching.

itens.enunciado: Describe the four steps the manual recommends for Part 6 (gapped text).
itens.modelo: 1. Read the base text first to understand the structure. 2. For each gap, note what comes before and after: reference words, time sequence, signalling nouns, contrasts. 3. Choose the paragraph that fits both sides and check that its reference words have a referent. 4. Do not rule out an option because it has been used; an earlier choice may be wrong.

criterios.ideia: Ver o que vem antes e depois da lacuna
Verificar que as palavras de referência têm referente

itens.explicacao: A Part 6 testa coesão, coerência e estrutura; há uma opção a mais.

itens.enunciado: How should you divide the 90 minutes of the Writing paper, and how should you choose the Part 2 task?
itens.modelo: About 45 minutes for each part: ten to plan, thirty to write and five to check. In Part 2, choose the task whose genre, reader and topic you can handle best, not the one with the most attractive topic.

criterios.ideia: Escolher pelo género/leitor/tema que se domina

itens.explicacao: A gestão do tempo e a escolha da tarefa são parte da estratégia de exame.

licao.resumo: A primeira prova simulada reproduz o formato completo do C2 Proficiency com material novo: Reading and Use of English (sete partes), Writing (ensaio sobre arte pública e três tarefas à escolha), Listening e Speaking. Deve ser feita em condições de exame, com tempo cronometrado. Neste módulo praticam-se itens das Parts 1 a 5 e do Writing Part 1, aplicando as estratégias de cada tarefa: testar cada opção na expressão completa (Part 1), decidir a classe de palavra e verificar ambos os lados da lacuna (Parts 2 e 3), identificar o que a palavra-chave obriga (Part 4) e formar uma resposta antes de ler as opções (Part 5).
pontos: Part 1: colocações e expressões fixas — take their toll, on the verge of, set great store by, the litmus test, a bone of contention, a far cry from.
Part 2: uma palavra por lacuna; alvos frequentes são preposições, what-clefts e expressões fixas (Even so, as though).
Part 3: muitas vezes mais do que uma mudança (PRODUCE → counterproductive; BREAK → unbroken).
Part 4: duas metades por item — can't have meant | to offend.
Part 5: rejeitar opções que contradizem, exageram ou atribuem mal; a última pergunta pode ser global.
Writing Part 1: resumir e avaliar todos os pontos de ambos os textos e desenvolver a opinião própria.
licao.exemplo: Part 5 (p. 236, chave p. 337): na pergunta 36, a opção 'It has made him a fundamentally more patient person' é contrariada pelo texto ('not because I had become a patient person, which I have not'); a certa é 'It has influenced, if modestly, how he approaches problems elsewhere'.

itens.enunciado: Part 1: 'Pollution and hunting had ____ their toll, and by the 1970s the animal was on the verge of disappearing.'
itens.explicacao: Take its/their toll = causar danos (chave: 1 A).
porque: Certo: take their toll.
Make não forma a expressão.
Paid sugere pagar portagem, mas a expressão é take its toll.
Give não forma a expressão.

itens.enunciado: Part 1: 'Ecologists, however, set great ____ by their reappearance.'
itens.explicacao: Set great store by = dar grande importância a (chave: 5 C).
porque: Value não forma a expressão fixa com set.
Price não forma a expressão.
Certo: set great store by.
Weight forma outra colocação (attach weight to), não com set by.

itens.enunciado: Part 1: 'For fish farmers… the otter has become a bone of ____.'
itens.explicacao: A bone of contention = motivo de discórdia (chave: 7 C).
porque: Dispute não forma a expressão fixa.
Argument não forma a expressão fixa.
Certo: a bone of contention.
Conflict não forma a expressão fixa.

itens.enunciado: Part 2 (open cloze), 'The private page'. Write one word for each gap, separated by commas: 'Most were never intended (9) ____ publication… (10) ____ makes a diary valuable to historians is precisely its lack of polish.'
itens.modelo: for, What
itens.explicacao: intended for publication; What makes a diary valuable… is… (wh-cleft).

itens.enunciado: Part 3 (word formation), 'The trouble with multitasking'. Write the words for: (18) 'a habit adopted to raise output turns out to be ____ (PRODUCE)'; (24) 'a period of ____ (BREAK) focus remains the most reliable route to quality'.
itens.modelo: (18) counterproductive (24) unbroken
itens.explicacao: Ambos exigem prefixo e sufixo/forma de particípio; o sentido negativo vem do texto inteiro.

itens.enunciado: Part 4. 'I'm sure she didn't intend to offend anyone.' MEANT → She ________ anyone.
itens.modelo: She can't have meant to offend anyone.
itens.explicacao: Dedução negativa no passado + mean to do (Unit 2).

itens.enunciado: Part 4. 'People say that the castle was built by the Moors.' SAID → The castle ________ by the Moors.
itens.modelo: The castle is said to have been built by the Moors.
itens.explicacao: Reporting passive com infinitivo perfeito passivo (Unit 4).

itens.enunciado: Part 4. 'He didn't apologise at all for the delay.' SLIGHTEST → He did ________ the delay.
itens.modelo: He did not offer the slightest apology for the delay.

criterios.ideia: the slightest apology for / in the slightest for

itens.explicacao: Expressão fixa com slightest; as duas metades pontuam separadamente.

itens.enunciado: Part 5. Read the extract from the personal essay 'The patience of old chairs' and answer the questions.
itens.excerto:
When I took up furniture restoration in my forties, I told friends it was a hobby, which was a way of lowering expectations, mainly my own. I had spent twenty years writing reports that were read once and filed. I wanted, I think, to make something that could be sat on.
The first lesson was humbling. My teacher, a retired cabinetmaker called Duarte, who had worked for the same workshop in Porto for thirty-eight years, handed me a chair with a broken stretcher and asked me what was wrong with it. I pointed to the break. He shook his head. The break, he explained, was the symptom; the problem was that someone, years before, had glued a loose joint instead of remaking it, and the strain had travelled along the frame until the weakest piece gave way. 'Most damage,' he said, 'is old repair.'

perguntas.enunciado: In the first paragraph, the writer suggests that he took up restoration partly because
opcoes: he wanted his work to have a more tangible result.
his friends had encouraged him to find a hobby.
he was dissatisfied with the quality of his reports.
he hoped to change his profession.
perguntas.explicacao: 'to make something that could be sat on' (chave: 31 A).
porque: Certo: queria fazer algo que se pudesse usar.
Ele próprio chamou-lhe hobby para baixar expectativas; os amigos não o incentivaram.
Critica o destino dos relatórios (lidos uma vez), não a sua qualidade.
Não diz que queria mudar de profissão.

perguntas.enunciado: What does Duarte's remark 'Most damage is old repair' refer to?
opcoes: the tendency of beginners to misdiagnose problems
the fragility of chairs made by inexperienced craftsmen
the way old furniture gradually weakens with use
harm caused by earlier attempts to fix a problem superficially
perguntas.explicacao: 'someone… had glued a loose joint instead of remaking it' (chave: 32 D).
porque: Duarte fala de reparações antigas, não de diagnósticos de principiantes.
Não fala de cadeiras mal feitas, mas de reparações mal feitas.
Não é o uso que enfraquece, é a reparação antiga.
Certo: colaram uma junta em vez de a refazer.

itens.explicacao: Questões 31–32 da prova simulada 1.

itens.enunciado: Part 5 (continued). Read another part of 'The patience of old chairs' and answer the questions.
itens.excerto:
Duarte was scathing about what he called 'dentist's work', the kind of refinishing that strips away a century of patina and leaves a piece looking like a reproduction of itself. A chair, in his view, should be allowed to admit its history. Not all his customers agreed. Some wanted their grandmother's sideboard to look as it had in a shop window in 1950, and he would occasionally turn the work down rather than do it.
There is a temptation, when writing about manual work, to sentimentalise it, and I am aware of having done so already. It is not all quiet satisfaction. Much of it is tedious, some of it is physically uncomfortable, and a good deal of it goes wrong. I have ruined more veneer than I care to admit. But the failures are instructive in a way that failures at a desk seldom are, because their causes are visible.

perguntas.enunciado: Duarte objected to 'dentist's work' because it
opcoes: was too expensive for most customers.
removed the evidence of a piece's age.
left visible marks of the repair.
required skills that few restorers possess.
perguntas.explicacao: 'strips away a century of patina' (chave: 34 B).
porque: Não se fala do custo para os clientes.
Certo: retira a pátina de um século.
Ele critica o contrário: a peça fica a parecer uma reprodução nova.
Não se fala de competências raras.

perguntas.enunciado: In the fifth paragraph, the writer
opcoes: argues that manual failures are more costly than intellectual ones.
regrets the time he has wasted on unsuccessful repairs.
claims that failure is less common in the workshop than at a desk.
admits that his account of manual work may have been idealised.
perguntas.explicacao: 'There is a temptation… to sentimentalise it, and I am aware of having done so' (chave: 35 D).
porque: Não diz que falhas manuais custam mais.
Admite falhas, mas não lamenta o tempo perdido.
Diz que as falhas são instrutivas, não menos frequentes.
Certo: admite ter idealizado o trabalho manual.

perguntas.enunciado: According to the writer, why are failures in the workshop more instructive than failures at a desk?
perguntas.modelo: Because their causes are visible: a joint that will not close tells you exactly what you did wrong.
perguntas.explicacao: A resposta está na última frase do excerto ('because their causes are visible').

itens.explicacao: Questões 34–35 da prova simulada 1 e uma pergunta aberta.

itens.enunciado: Writing Part 1. Text 1 (Art in public places): public art reaches people who never visit galleries, gives places an identity, the arguments it provokes bring residents into a conversation about their town, its cost is modest compared with a road junction, and a town without it chooses to be anonymous. Text 2 (Whose art?): too much public art is chosen by experts and imposed on residents who were never asked, who resent it because the money could have paid for services; it is valuable only when the community helps to choose or make it. Write an essay of 240–280 words summarising and evaluating the key points of both texts and developing your own view.
itens.modelo: Public art divides opinion more sharply than most items in a council budget, and the two texts take opposite views of why that matters. The first writer defends works of art in streets and squares. Such works are seen by people who would not normally visit a gallery; they give character to places that would otherwise have none; and the disputes they cause draw local people into a debate about the future of their town. Their price is small beside that of ordinary roadworks. The argument about reaching a wider audience is persuasive, and so is the idea that controversy can be productive. The final claim, however, that a town without such works has opted for anonymity, is overstated: character can come from architecture, markets or landscape as much as from sculpture. The second writer does not reject public art but questions the way it is selected. When experts choose a piece and residents are simply presented with it, resentment follows naturally, particularly if the funds could have paid for basic services. Art of this kind justifies itself only when the community helps to choose or create it. This is a fair criticism of a common practice, although it risks assuming that local preferences will always be wiser than expert judgement. In my view, the two positions can be reconciled. Public art deserves funding precisely because everyone encounters it, but for the same reason everyone should have a say in it.

criterios.ideia: Pontos do Texto 1 (público alargado, identidade, debate, custo modesto, anonimato)
Pontos do Texto 2 (imposta por peritos, dinheiro desviado de serviços, envolvimento da comunidade)

itens.explicacao: O ensaio-modelo (p. 338) tem banda 5 em todas as subescalas: todos os pontos resumidos e avaliados, opinião desenvolvida a partir dos dois textos.

licao.resumo: A segunda prova simulada segue o mesmo formato completo do C2 Proficiency. O Reading and Use of English trata pedidos de desculpa de empresas (Part 1), cidades caminháveis (Part 2), legendas de museus (Part 3) e um livro de memórias sobre aprender português aos quarenta e um anos (Part 5); o Writing Part 1 compara competição e cooperação na escola. Neste módulo praticam-se itens destas partes, com as mesmas estratégias: colocações e expressões fixas, classe de palavra e mudanças múltiplas, as duas metades da Part 4 e a localização do passo relevante antes de ler as opções.
pontos: Part 1: make or break, hedged with conditions, see through, pay lip service to, own up to, make excuses, set out, from the heart.
Part 2: Unlike…, in their own right, with cars in mind, even, more than, none of these, one corner at a time.
Part 3: KNOW → unknown; PENETRATE → impenetrable; TRIVIAL → trivialising; USE → useless; SCHOLAR → scholarly.
Part 4: If only I had accepted…; No sooner had she left than…; came as a surprise to…; may have been destroyed.
Part 5: as respostas certas parafraseiam o texto; distratores repetem palavras mudando a relação.
Writing Part 1: um bom ensaio nota que as posições estão mais próximas do que parecem e combina-as com uma razão.
licao.exemplo: Part 5, pergunta 33 (p. 250, chave p. 341): Dona Ermelinda ajudou porque 'she did not slow down or simplify… she did not seem to mind' — expôs o narrador ao discurso natural sem o pressionar; a opção 'she adapted her language to his level' contradiz o texto.

itens.enunciado: Part 1: 'Customers are quick to ____ through statements that pay lip service to their concerns.'
itens.explicacao: See through = perceber a falta de sinceridade (chave: 3 D).
porque: Look through é folhear, não perceber falsidade.
Notice through não existe.
Spot through não existe.
Certo: see through = perceber a falta de sinceridade.

itens.enunciado: Part 1: 'An apology that comes too late, or that is ____ with conditions, often does more harm than good.'
itens.explicacao: Hedged with conditions = rodeado de condições (chave: 2 B).
porque: Fenced with conditions não é a colocação.
Certo: hedged with conditions.
Walled não colocaliza com conditions.
Bordered não colocaliza com conditions.

itens.enunciado: Part 1: 'it owns ____ to the mistake, it explains what went wrong without making excuses'
itens.explicacao: Own up to = admitir (chave: 5 B).
porque: Own in não existe.
Certo: own up to = admitir.
Own out não existe.
Own off não existe.

itens.enunciado: Part 2 (open cloze), 'In praise of walking cities'. Write one word for each gap, separated by commas: '(9) ____ the driver, who sees streets as obstacles…, the walker experiences them as places in (10) ____ own right.'
itens.modelo: Unlike, their
itens.explicacao: Unlike introduz o contraste; in their own right é expressão fixa.

itens.enunciado: Part 3 (word formation), 'Rethinking the museum label'. Write the words for: (18) 'many visitors found them ____ (PENETRATE)'; (21) 'risk ____ (TRIVIAL) the objects they describe'.
itens.modelo: (18) impenetrable (21) trivialising
itens.explicacao: (18) prefixo im- + sufixo -able; (21) risk + -ing com verbo derivado em -ise.

itens.enunciado: Part 4. 'I regret not accepting the job in Lisbon.' ONLY → If ________ the job in Lisbon.
itens.modelo: If only I had accepted the job in Lisbon.
itens.explicacao: If only + past perfect para arrependimento sobre o passado (Unit 3).

itens.enunciado: Part 4. 'Everyone was surprised that he resigned.' CAME → His resignation ________ everyone.
itens.modelo: His resignation came as a surprise to everyone.
itens.explicacao: Expressão fixa: come as a surprise to somebody.

itens.enunciado: Part 4. 'I didn't realise how much work the project involved.' IDEA → I had ________ work the project involved.
itens.modelo: I had no idea how much work the project involved.
itens.explicacao: Have no idea + pergunta indireta.

itens.enunciado: Part 5. Read the extract from the memoir 'Late Portuguese' and answer the questions.
itens.excerto:
The first months were spent in a state I came to think of as polite deafness. I could buy bread and ask for the bill, but conversation passed over me like weather. Portuguese, as spoken in Lisbon, swallows its vowels; whole syllables that I had learnt from the book simply failed to appear. I would rehearse a question on the way to the café, ask it perfectly, and then understand nothing of the answer, which was usually friendly and always fast. At work, meetings were held in English for my benefit, which was kind and entirely counterproductive.
What changed things was not a course, though I took several, but a neighbour. Dona Ermelinda was eighty, lived on the floor below, and had decided, without consulting me, that I was too thin. She began leaving soup at my door, and when I went down to return the pots, she talked. She talked about her late husband, the price of fish, the scandal of the new tram timetable, and she did not slow down or simplify anything for my benefit. I understood perhaps a tenth of it. But she did not seem to mind, and after a while I stopped minding too.

perguntas.enunciado: What does the writer mean by 'polite deafness'?
opcoes: He pretended not to understand in order to avoid conversation.
He was too shy to ask people to repeat themselves.
He could manage simple exchanges but could not follow real conversation.
He found local people unwilling to talk to him.
perguntas.explicacao: 'I could buy bread… but conversation passed over me' (chave: 32 C).
porque: Ele não fingia; não conseguia acompanhar.
O texto não fala de timidez em pedir para repetir.
Certo: trocas simples sim, conversa real não.
As pessoas falavam com ele, amigavelmente.

perguntas.enunciado: Dona Ermelinda's conversations were helpful because
opcoes: she adapted her language to his level.
she taught him the vocabulary he needed in daily life.
she exposed him to natural speech, without pressure.
perguntas.explicacao: 'she did not slow down or simplify… she did not seem to mind' (chave: 33 D).
porque: Ela não abrandava nem simplificava.
O texto não diz que ela o corrigia.
Falava de tudo, sem ensinar vocabulário.
Certo: fala natural sem pressão.

perguntas.enunciado: Why does the writer describe the meetings held in English as 'kind and entirely counterproductive'?
perguntas.modelo: They were kind because colleagues wanted to help him, but counterproductive because they deprived him of the exposure to Portuguese he needed in order to learn.
perguntas.explicacao: A inferência deve poder ligar-se ao texto: as reuniões em inglês tiravam-lhe contacto com a língua.

itens.explicacao: Questões 32–33 da prova simulada 2 e uma pergunta de inferência.

itens.enunciado: Part 5 (continued). Read another part of 'Late Portuguese' and answer the questions.
itens.excerto:
I have read since that adults learn languages less efficiently than children, and I do not doubt it. But the comparison misses something. A child learns without knowing what it is losing; an adult learns in full awareness of being, for a long time, a diminished version of himself. In English I am, I like to think, reasonably articulate. In Portuguese I was, for two years, a man who could not make a joke, could not disagree subtly, could not tell a story without the ending collapsing into gestures.
It was also, though I only saw this later, an education in attention. Because I could not rely on words, I learnt to watch faces, to notice tone, to wait. Dona Ermelinda's stories had a shape I could follow long before I could follow the sentences: a rising indignation, a pause, a punchline delivered with a flat hand on the table. I began to anticipate the pause.

perguntas.enunciado: In the fourth paragraph, the writer argues that adult learners
opcoes: learn more efficiently than research suggests.
are conscious of losing the identity their first language gives them.
should avoid comparing themselves with children.
need a strong sense of self-esteem in order to succeed.
perguntas.explicacao: 'in full awareness of being… a diminished version of himself' (chave: 34 B).
porque: Ele aceita que os adultos aprendem menos eficientemente.
Certo: consciência de ser uma versão diminuída de si.
Ele faz a comparação com crianças; não diz para a evitar.
Diz que não recomendaria a quem depende de ser compreendido, não que é preciso autoestima.

perguntas.enunciado: What does the writer say he gained from his difficulties?
opcoes: an ability to read meaning beyond words
a better understanding of Portuguese humour
a closer friendship with his colleagues
perguntas.explicacao: 'I learnt to watch faces, to notice tone' (chave: 35 A).
porque: Certo: aprendeu a ler rostos e tom.
Não fala de humor português em geral.
Diz que não conseguia contar histórias.
Não fala de amizade com colegas.

itens.explicacao: Questões 34–35 da prova simulada 2.

itens.enunciado: Writing Part 1. Text 1 (The case for competition): children compete anyway, school is a place to learn to win and lose with grace, comparison raises standards, the danger is competitions only a few can win. Text 2 (Learning together): public rankings tell most pupils they are not good enough and teach that effort is pointless; cooperation rewards all contributors and reflects adult teamwork; pupils should be measured against their own earlier performance. Write an essay of 240–280 words summarising and evaluating both texts and developing your own view.
itens.modelo: Few questions in education provoke as much feeling as the place of competition, and the two texts reach opposite conclusions from a shared concern for pupils. The first writer argues that rivalry is already part of children's lives and that school offers a safe setting in which to learn how to handle both success and failure. Being compared with classmates also makes pupils more careful with their work. The writer concedes, however, that contests which almost nobody can win do real harm. The point about learning to lose gracefully is convincing, and the concession is important, since it moves the argument from whether pupils should compete to how. The second writer focuses on what public rankings do to the majority. Such lists tell most children that they are failing and so discourage effort, whereas cooperation rewards all who contribute and reflects the teamwork of adult life. This is not a case for lower standards but for judging each pupil against his or her own earlier performance. This is persuasive, although the claim that adults mostly work in teams is a generalisation. The two positions are closer than they first appear. In my view, the most sensible approach combines them: competition in low-stakes settings, such as sport or quizzes, where losing teaches resilience, and assessment based on individual progress where a child's confidence is at stake.

criterios.ideia: Pontos do Texto 1 (competem de qualquer forma, ganhar e perder, padrões, concessão)
Pontos do Texto 2 (rankings desmotivam, cooperação, trabalho em equipa, progresso individual)

itens.explicacao: Ensaio-modelo da chave (p. 342): ambos rejeitam concursos que só poucos ganham; a posição pessoal combina-os.

licao.resumo: A terceira prova simulada completa o treino do C2 Proficiency. O Reading and Use of English trata a apicultura urbana (Part 1), o mito da pessoa matinal (Part 2), as bibliotecas de objetos (Part 3) e um ensaio de uma cartógrafa sobre o que os mapas deixam de fora (Part 5); o Writing Part 1 discute se os famosos devem ser modelos. Neste módulo praticam-se itens destas partes, aplicando as estratégias de cada tarefa, com especial atenção às perguntas de atitude e de sentido global na Part 5.
pontos: Part 1: take off, at a premium, a status symbol, it stands to reason, in decline, few and far between, by the same token, bring to light.
Part 2: who claim…, far from conclusive, more harm than good, however many hours, If we judged…, go on ruling.
Part 3: OBSERVE → observation; ACCESS → accessible; PROBLEM → unproblematic; LOSE → loss; EXPECT → unexpected.
Part 4: is believed to have been stolen; would rather you didn't smoke; was a low turnout at; has little in common with.
Part 5: a última pergunta é global (atitude geral); 'None of this means that we should go back… But I wish…' indica aceitação com reservas.
Writing Part 1: avaliar cada ponto com uma razão e propor uma posição que vá além de concordar com um dos textos.
licao.exemplo: Part 5, pergunta 35 (p. 265, chave p. 345): 'the most persuasive argument a map has ever made' significa que, ao parecerem neutros ('It presents itself as neutral'), os mapas digitais fazem as suas escolhas parecer naturais.

itens.enunciado: Part 1: 'It ____ to reason, supporters argue, that more bees mean better pollination.'
itens.explicacao: It stands to reason = é lógico (chave: 4 D).
porque: Holds não forma a expressão.
Makes não forma a expressão.
Comes não forma a expressão.
Certo: it stands to reason.

itens.enunciado: Part 1: 'in cities where green spaces are few and far ____, the competition can be fierce.'
itens.explicacao: Few and far between = raros (chave: 6 B).
porque: Few and far apart não é a expressão.
Certo: few and far between.
Among não forma a expressão.
Beyond não forma a expressão.

itens.enunciado: Part 1: 'Studies bringing such risks to ____ have received far less attention than the hives themselves.'
itens.explicacao: Bring something to light = revelar (chave: 8 C).
porque: Surface não forma a expressão com bring to.
Bring to view não é a expressão fixa.
Certo: bring to light.
Notice usa-se em bring to someone's notice, outra estrutura.

itens.enunciado: Part 2 (open cloze), 'The myth of the morning person'. Write one word for each gap, separated by commas: 'the evidence that getting up early makes people more productive is (10) ____ from conclusive… forcing a night owl to work at six may do more harm (11) ____ good.'
itens.modelo: far, than
itens.explicacao: far from conclusive; do more harm than good (expressões fixas).

itens.enunciado: Part 3 (word formation), 'Libraries of things'. Write the words for: (21) 'Running such a library is not entirely ____ (PROBLEM)'; (23) 'organisers report remarkably low rates of ____ (LOSE)'.
itens.modelo: (21) unproblematic (23) loss
itens.explicacao: (21) prefixo negativo + sufixo adjetival; (23) mudança interna lose → loss.

itens.enunciado: Part 4. 'People think that the painting was stolen in 1985.' BELIEVED → The painting ________ in 1985.
itens.modelo: The painting is believed to have been stolen in 1985.
itens.explicacao: Reporting passive com infinitivo perfeito passivo.

itens.enunciado: Part 4. 'Hardly anybody came to the meeting.' TURNOUT → There ________ the meeting.
itens.modelo: There was a very low turnout at the meeting.
itens.explicacao: Colocação: a low/poor turnout.

itens.enunciado: Part 4. 'The new manager is very different from the old one.' COMMON → The new manager ________ the old one.
itens.modelo: The new manager has very little in common with the old one.
itens.explicacao: Expressão fixa: have little in common with.

itens.enunciado: Part 5. Read the extract from 'What the map leaves out' and answer the questions.
itens.excerto:
A map cannot show everything. Even the most detailed street plan leaves out far more than it includes: the smell of the bakery, the steepness that makes a street unbearable in August, the corner where everyone knows not to linger at night. The cartographer chooses, and every choice is a judgement about what matters. When I was learning, my teacher made us draw the same village three times, once for a walker, once for a tax inspector and once for a child, and then asked us which was the true one. The walker's map was all paths and gradients; the inspector's was all boundaries; the child's had the sweet shop at the centre and the church nowhere at all. The answer, of course, was that none of them was, or all of them were.
Digital maps have not removed these choices; they have hidden them. Because they can zoom endlessly, they give the impression of containing everything, of being not a description of the world but the world itself. The decisions are still made, but by algorithms and commercial agreements that nobody sees.

perguntas.enunciado: Her teacher's exercise was designed to show that
opcoes: maps should always be adapted to the needs of their users.
children understand maps better than adults.
tax maps were more accurate than others.
every map reflects a particular purpose and none is complete.
perguntas.explicacao: 'which was the true one… none of them was, or all of them were' (chave: 32 D).
porque: O exercício mostra que nenhum mapa é completo, não que se devem adaptar.
Não compara crianças e adultos.
O mapa do inspetor não é apresentado como mais exato.
Certo: cada mapa tem um propósito e nenhum é completo.

perguntas.enunciado: According to the third paragraph, digital maps
opcoes: contain fewer choices than paper maps.
are less detailed than they appear.
perguntas.explicacao: 'Digital maps have not removed these choices; they have hidden them' (chave: 33 A).
porque: Certo: escondem as decisões.
As escolhas continuam; estão só escondidas.
O autor diz que dão impressão de conter tudo, não que têm menos detalhe.
Não diz que enganam deliberadamente; diz que escondem a autoria.

itens.explicacao: Questões 32–33 da prova simulada 3.

itens.enunciado: Part 5 (continued). Read the end of 'What the map leaves out' and answer the questions.
itens.excerto:
A paper map announced its maker. It had a title, a date, a scale and, often, a name in the corner. Some makers hid small inventions in their work, a street that did not exist or a hamlet that nobody lived in, so that copies could be detected. Even these traps were a kind of signature. You knew that someone had drawn it, and you could ask what that person had wanted you to see. The screen in your hand has no corner and no name. It presents itself as neutral, and that, I think, is the most persuasive argument a map has ever made.
None of this means that we should go back. I use digital maps every day, and I would not want to find my way around an unfamiliar city without one. I have followed one, on a bad day, into a dead end, and blamed myself rather than the map. But I wish they came with a small reminder, somewhere on the screen, that they too were drawn by someone, for someone, and that what they leave out may matter as much as what they show.

perguntas.enunciado: What does the writer mean by 'the most persuasive argument a map has ever made'?
opcoes: Digital maps convince users because they are accurate.
By appearing neutral, digital maps make their choices seem natural.
Paper maps were better at persuading their readers.
Maps should always include the name of their maker.
perguntas.explicacao: 'It presents itself as neutral' (chave: 35 B).
porque: O autor diz que a sua preocupação não é a exatidão, mas a autoria.
Certo: ao parecer neutro, torna as escolhas naturais.
Fala do mapa digital, não do de papel.
Pede um lembrete de autoria, mas não é o sentido da frase.

perguntas.enunciado: What is the writer's overall attitude to digital maps?
perguntas.explicacao: 'None of this means that we should go back… But I wish…' (chave: 36 D).
porque: Usa-os todos os dias; não os rejeita.
Critica-os: não há entusiasmo acrítico.
Recusa romantizar o mapa de papel.
Certo: 'None of this means… But I wish…'.

perguntas.enunciado: Why does the writer describe the invented streets and hamlets on paper maps as 'a kind of signature'?
perguntas.modelo: Because they showed that a particular person had made the map: they marked its authorship, so readers knew someone had drawn it and could ask what that person wanted them to see.

criterios.ideia: Marcavam a autoria / mostravam que alguém fez o mapa
Permitiam detetar cópias / perguntar pela intenção

perguntas.explicacao: A ideia central do texto é a autoria, que torna possível a discordância.

itens.explicacao: Questões 35–36 da prova simulada 3 e uma pergunta aberta.

itens.enunciado: Writing Part 1. Text 1 (Famous examples): public figures shape young people's ambitions and can change attitudes faster than government campaigns, so fame brings obligations; those who complain chose the spotlight. Text 2 (Closer to home): celebrity success is narrow, due to talent or luck, and reaches us through managed images; young people learn more from adults they know; holding celebrities to moral standards distracts us from ordinary examples. Write an essay of 240–280 words summarising and evaluating both texts and developing your own view.
itens.modelo: Both texts accept that young people need examples to follow; they disagree about where to find them and what we may ask of them. The first writer argues that celebrities, willingly or not, influence what young people hope to become, and that a single gesture, such as a sportsman admitting to depression, can shift attitudes more quickly than official campaigns. Influence of this kind carries duties as well as advantages, and stars who resent the burden should recall that their visibility was their own choice. Their reach is hard to dispute. The claim that fame is always chosen is less convincing: many athletes and musicians become well known as teenagers, before they could understand what celebrity demands. The second writer shifts the focus from the famous to the familiar. Celebrity success is narrow, often owed to rare gifts or luck, and reaches the public in carefully controlled form; the adults in a young person's daily life are more instructive. Expecting moral perfection from stars blinds us to the worth of these everyday models. This is a persuasive corrective, although it may underestimate how much a distant figure can inspire someone whose surroundings offer few examples. In my view, both writers are partly right. Famous people do have unusual influence, but treating them as the main source of moral guidance is a mistake. Schools and communities would do better to make ordinary achievements visible.

criterios.ideia: Pontos do Texto 1 (influência, mais rápida que campanhas, obrigações, escolheram a fama)
Pontos do Texto 2 (sucesso estreito, sorte/talento, imagens geridas, adultos próximos, distração)
Paráfrase e ligação entre os textos

itens.explicacao: Ensaio-modelo da chave (p. 346): avalia cada texto com uma razão e propõe tornar visíveis as conquistas comuns.

modulos.titulo: 10.º ano (B1) — A world of many languages

licao.resumo: Um Mundo de Muitas Línguas (AE 10.º, B1): vocabulário para falar de línguas, present simple e continuous, nomes contáveis e incontáveis, e leitura de textos sobre o inglês no mundo.
pontos: Words about languages: Para falar de línguas usa-se: mother tongue (língua materna), native speaker (falante nativo), bilingual (bilingue), fluent (fluente), accent (sotaque), official language (língua oficial) e lingua franca (língua comum entre falantes de línguas diferentes).
Present simple vs continuous: O present simple exprime hábitos, rotinas e verdades gerais (She speaks three languages).
Countable and uncountable: Os nomes contáveis têm plural (a word, two words);
Reading: English worldwide: Nas perguntas de leitura, lê primeiro as perguntas, depois o texto, e procura o passo exato que justifica cada resposta.
licao.exemplo: Ana is bilingual: Portuguese is her mother tongue and she is fluent in English.

itens.enunciado: A person who speaks two languages equally well since childhood is ____.
itens.explicacao: Bilingual descreve quem domina duas línguas desde cedo.
porque: Certo: bilingual = fala duas línguas como se fossem ambas maternas.
fluent = fala bem uma língua, mas não diz que são duas.
native = falante nativo de uma língua; não indica duas.
monolingual = fala só uma língua.

itens.enunciado: Which word means 'sotaque'?
itens.explicacao: Accent é a pronúncia típica de um lugar: a Scottish accent.
porque: dialect = dialeto, uma variedade com vocabulário e gramática próprios, não só pronúncia.
accident = acidente; falso amigo pela forma.
speech = fala ou discurso, não o sotaque.
Certo: accent = maneira de pronunciar típica de uma região ou país.

itens.enunciado: 'Mother tongue' means the first language you learn as a child.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. Mother tongue = língua materna, a primeira que se aprende em casa.

itens.enunciado: Complete with ONE word: 'In Canada, English and French are the two ____ languages.'
itens.modelo: official
itens.explicacao: No Canadá, inglês e francês são as duas línguas oficiais (official languages).

itens.enunciado: Complete with the missing preposition: 'After a year at a Dublin school, Marta is now fluent ____ English.'
itens.modelo: in
itens.explicacao: Diz-se fluent in + língua; «fluent on» ou «fluent at» são erros frequentes.

itens.enunciado: In one sentence (10–20 words), explain why English is called a global language.
itens.modelo: English is a global language because people from many countries use it to communicate in business, travel and online.

criterios.ideia: Pessoas de países diferentes usam-no para comunicar

itens.explicacao: Uma boa resposta diz quem usa o inglês (pessoas de muitos países) e para quê (trabalho, ciência, viagens, internet).

itens.enunciado: 'Look! Our teacher ____ to the new student in Chinese.'
itens.explicacao: Look!, Listen! e now pedem o present continuous.
porque: O present simple descreve hábitos, não o que se vê neste momento.
Certo: 'Look!' mostra uma ação a decorrer agora: present continuous.
Has talked é present perfect; 'Look!' pede uma ação em curso.
O past simple fala do passado; 'Look!' indica agora.

itens.enunciado: 'My cousin ____ three languages: Portuguese, English and French.'
itens.explicacao: Factos permanentes usam o present simple: she speaks.
porque: Falta o -s da 3.ª pessoa do singular (my cousin = he/she).
A forma contínua indicaria que está a falar agora, não que sabe as línguas.
'are' não concorda com 'my cousin' e a forma contínua não serve.
Certo: Capacidade permanente: present simple, com -s na 3.ª pessoa.

itens.enunciado: 'I am knowing the answer' is correct English.
itens.explicacao: Falso. Know é um verbo de estado: diz-se 'I know the answer'.

itens.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets: 'This term, Rui ____ (learn) Spanish online.'
itens.modelo: is learning
itens.explicacao: 'This term' indica uma situação temporária: is learning.

itens.enunciado: Complete with the correct negative form of the verb in brackets: 'My grandmother ____ (not/understand) English, so I translate for her.'
itens.modelo: doesn't understand
itens.explicacao: Understand é verbo de estado e a frase descreve um facto geral: doesn't understand.

itens.enunciado: Correct the mistake: 'Listen! Somebody sings in the next room.' →
itens.modelo: Listen! Somebody is singing in the next room.
itens.explicacao: 'Listen!' mostra que a ação está a acontecer agora: is singing.

itens.enunciado: 'How ____ languages does your teacher speak?'
itens.explicacao: How many + plural contável; how much + incontável.
porque: Certo: Languages é contável e está no plural: how many.
Much usa-se com incontáveis (much time).
'How lot' não existe; seria 'a lot of'.
A little usa-se com incontáveis e não depois de how.

itens.enunciado: Which sentence is correct?
opcoes: She gave me an useful advice.
She gave me a useful advices.
She gave me some useful advice.
She gave me some useful advices.
itens.explicacao: Some advice ou a piece of advice.
porque: Advice não leva a/an e 'useful' começa por som /j/, por isso seria 'a'.
Mistura 'a' com plural, e advice não tem plural.
Certo: Advice é incontável: sem -s e sem a/an.
Advice não tem plural.

itens.enunciado: 'There is only a little time before the exam' means there is some time, but not much.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. A little = algum, pouco, mas suficiente; little sozinho tem sentido mais negativo.

itens.enunciado: Complete with ONE quantifier: 'We didn't get ____ information about the exchange programme, so we sent an e-mail.'
itens.modelo: much

criterios.ideia: Quantificador para incontável em frase negativa

itens.explicacao: Information é incontável: em frases negativas usa-se much ou any.

itens.enunciado: Correct the mistake: 'I have a lot of homeworks this weekend.' →
itens.modelo: I have a lot of homework this weekend.
itens.explicacao: Homework é incontável: nunca leva -s.

itens.enunciado: 'There are ____ students from Ukraine in our school this year, so we help them with Portuguese.'
itens.explicacao: A few + plural contável; a little + incontável.
porque: Little usa-se com incontáveis e tem sentido negativo.
Certo: Students é contável no plural: a few.
A little usa-se com incontáveis.
Much usa-se com incontáveis.

itens.enunciado: In 'Many teenagers play games online. This helps them learn English', 'This' refers to playing games online.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. This retoma a ideia inteira da frase anterior: jogar online.

itens.enunciado: In a multiple-choice reading question, what is the best first step?
opcoes: Choose the option that repeats the largest number of words from the text.
Read the question and find the part of the text it refers to.
Translate the whole text into Portuguese before answering.
Read only the first and the last paragraphs of the text.
itens.explicacao: Primeiro localiza; depois compara cada opção com esse passo.
porque: As opções que repetem palavras do texto são muitas vezes armadilhas.
Certo: Localizar o passo certo é a base de qualquer resposta de leitura.
Traduzir tudo gasta tempo e não ajuda a escolher.
A resposta pode estar em qualquer parágrafo.

itens.enunciado: Read the text and answer the questions.
itens.excerto: When Tiago started secondary school in Coimbra, English was just another subject for him. Then he discovered online games. Every evening he played with teenagers from Poland, Brazil and South Korea, and the only language they all shared was English. 'At first I only knew a few words, like help and attack,' he laughs. 'Now I can have a real conversation.' Tiago is not unusual. Many young Europeans learn a lot of English outside the classroom, through music, series and video games. Teachers welcome this, but they also warn that the English of games and chats is very informal. 'Students write u instead of you in their essays,' says one teacher. For Tiago, the solution is simple: he uses one kind of English with his friends online and another kind at school. 'It's like having two wardrobes,' he says, 'one for the weekend and one for job interviews.'

perguntas.enunciado: How did Tiago improve his English?
opcoes: By watching series in English with his teachers
By living in Poland and in Brazil for a year
By playing online games with teenagers from other countries
By studying grammar with a private teacher every single evening
perguntas.explicacao: Every evening he played with teenagers from Poland, Brazil and South Korea.
porque: Os professores não veem séries com ele.
Ele joga com pessoas desses países, não viveu lá.
Certo: O texto diz que jogava todas as noites com adolescentes de vários países.
O texto não fala de explicador; ele aprende a jogar.

perguntas.enunciado: Teachers think the English students learn online is always suitable for school essays.
perguntas.explicacao: Falso. Os professores avisam que esse inglês é muito informal (u em vez de you).

perguntas.enunciado: Which word in the text means 'relaxed, not formal'?
perguntas.modelo: informal
perguntas.explicacao: 'the English of games and chats is very informal'.

perguntas.enunciado: What does Tiago mean by 'having two wardrobes'?
opcoes: He adapts his English to the situation.
He prefers informal English to school English.
He has more clothes than his friends.
He needs two languages to get a job.
perguntas.explicacao: A metáfora do guarda-roupa compara registos a roupa para ocasiões diferentes.
porque: Certo: Tem um inglês para os amigos e outro para a escola: adapta o registo.
Ele não diz que prefere um; usa cada um no seu lugar.
É uma imagem; não fala de roupa real.
Fala de dois tipos de inglês, não de duas línguas.

itens.explicacao: Lê o texto com atenção e volta ao passo exato antes de responder.

itens.enunciado: Read the text and answer the questions.
itens.excerto: English is an official language in countries as different as Ireland, Nigeria, India and Canada. However, most people who speak English today are not native speakers. They learned it at school, at work or on the internet, and they use it to talk to people from other countries. In this situation English works as a lingua franca. Some experts say that this is changing the language itself. When a Portuguese engineer and a Japanese engineer discuss a project in English, nobody checks whether they use British or American expressions; what matters is that they understand each other. For language learners, this is good news. It means that the goal is not to sound exactly like a person from London or New York, but to communicate clearly.

perguntas.enunciado: According to the text, most English speakers today…
opcoes: were born in English-speaking countries like Britain or the USA.
speak only British English at work.
learned English as a second or foreign language.
perguntas.explicacao: A maioria aprendeu-o na escola, no trabalho ou na internet.
porque: O texto diz o contrário: a maioria não é nativa.
Usam-no também no trabalho e na internet.
O texto diz que ninguém verifica se as expressões são britânicas ou americanas.
Certo: 'most people who speak English today are not native speakers'.

perguntas.enunciado: The writer thinks learners should try to sound exactly like people from London.
perguntas.explicacao: Falso. 'the goal is not to sound exactly like a person from London… but to communicate clearly'.

perguntas.enunciado: Which expression in the text means 'a common language used by people with different first languages'?
perguntas.modelo: lingua franca
perguntas.explicacao: 'English works as a lingua franca'.

perguntas.enunciado: What does 'they' refer to in 'what matters is that they understand each other'?
perguntas.explicacao: They retoma 'a Portuguese engineer and a Japanese engineer'.
porque: Certo: A frase fala do engenheiro português e do japonês.
Os especialistas estão noutra frase.
Os britânicos e americanos só aparecem como tipo de expressões.
Os falantes nativos não estão nesta frase.

itens.explicacao: Lê o texto com atenção e volta ao passo exato antes de responder.

licao.resumo: O Mundo Tecnológico (AE 10.º, B1): vocabulário de tecnologia, past simple e past continuous, present perfect vs past simple e phrasal verbs do dia a dia digital.
pontos: Technology vocabulary: Vocabulário essencial: device (dispositivo), screen (ecrã), app, download/upload (descarregar/carregar), password (palavra-passe), charger (carregador), update (atualização), invention (invenção), robot e artificial intelligence (inteligência artificial).
Past simple vs continuous: O past simple conta ações concluídas no passado (I bought a laptop).

Present perfect vs past simple: O present perfect (have/has + particípio) liga o passado ao presente: experiências sem data (I have used a 3D printer), resultados agora (I've lost my charger) e períodos que continuam (since, for, yet, already, ever, never).

Tech phrasal verbs: Phrasal verbs frequentes no mundo digital: log in/log out (entrar/sair da conta), switch on/off ou turn on/off (ligar/desligar), plug in (ligar à corrente), set up (configurar), back up (fazer cópia de segurança), turn up/down (aumentar/baixar o volume).
licao.exemplo: Before you download a new app, check that your device has the latest update.

itens.enunciado: You need a ____ to give your phone more battery.
itens.explicacao: Charger dá energia à bateria.
porque: screen = ecrã.
keyboard = teclado.
Certo: charger = carregador.
password = palavra-passe; não dá bateria.

itens.enunciado: 'Graham Bell ____ the telephone in the 1870s.'
itens.explicacao: Inventa-se uma máquina; descobre-se algo que já existe.
porque: Discover = encontrar algo que já existia (uma ilha, uma lei da natureza).
Certo: Invent = criar algo que não existia, como o telefone.
Find = encontrar algo perdido ou escondido.
Search = procurar.

itens.enunciado: To 'upload' a photo means to send it from your device to a website or app.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. Upload = enviar para a internet; download = trazer da internet para o dispositivo.

itens.enunciado: Complete with ONE word: 'Never share your ____ with anyone: it protects your account.'
itens.modelo: password
itens.explicacao: Password é a palavra-passe que protege uma conta.

itens.enunciado: Write the noun that comes from the verb: 'invent' → 'an ____'
itens.modelo: invention
itens.explicacao: Invent → invention (o objeto ou ideia) → inventor (a pessoa).

itens.enunciado: 'I ____ a film on my tablet when the internet stopped working.'
itens.explicacao: A ação longa vai para o continuous; a interrupção para o simple.
porque: Certo: Ação em curso interrompida: past continuous.
O past simple seria a ação curta; aqui a ação longa estava em curso.
Were não concorda com I.
Am watching é presente.

itens.enunciado: 'Last year my parents ____ me a new laptop for my birthday.'
itens.explicacao: Last year, yesterday e ago pedem o past simple.
porque: O continuous não serve para uma ação curta e concluída.
Certo: 'Last year' = passado concluído: past simple.
Buy é presente.
O present perfect não combina com 'last year'.

itens.enunciado: In 'While she was texting, she walked into a door', the texting was in progress when she walked into the door.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. While + past continuous mostra a ação em curso; walked é o acontecimento curto.

itens.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets: 'When the teacher came in, we ____ (play) a game on our phones.'
itens.modelo: were playing
itens.explicacao: A ação estava em curso quando o professor entrou: were playing.

itens.enunciado: Complete with the past simple of the verb in brackets: 'Yesterday I ____ (send) forty messages!'
itens.modelo: sent
itens.explicacao: Send é irregular: send – sent – sent.

itens.enunciado: Correct the mistake: 'I was losing my phone yesterday on the bus.' →
itens.modelo: I lost my phone yesterday on the bus.

criterios.ideia: Past simple para ação curta e concluída

itens.explicacao: Perder o telemóvel é uma ação curta e concluída: past simple.

itens.enunciado: '____ you ever ____ a virtual reality headset?'
itens.explicacao: Have you ever + particípio?
porque: Depois de have vem o particípio (used), não o infinitivo.
Certo: Ever + experiência sem data: present perfect (have + particípio).
Did pede o infinitivo (did you use), e ever pede present perfect.
O past continuous não serve para experiências de vida.

itens.enunciado: 'We ____ our new robot to the science fair two weeks ago.'
itens.explicacao: Ago pede sempre o past simple.
porque: Certo: 'two weeks ago' = passado terminado: past simple.
Took é o past simple; o particípio é taken.
Take é presente.
O present perfect não se usa com ago.

itens.enunciado: 'I have bought this phone in 2022' is correct.
itens.explicacao: Falso. Com 'in 2022' (data terminada) usa-se o past simple: I bought this phone in 2022.

itens.enunciado: Complete with the present perfect of the verb in brackets: 'My brother ____ (not/finish) his coding course yet.'
itens.modelo: hasn't finished
itens.explicacao: Yet em frase negativa pede o present perfect: hasn't finished.

itens.enunciado: Complete with ONE time word: 'I have had this smartwatch ____ my last birthday.'
itens.modelo: since

criterios.ideia: Palavra de tempo + ponto de partida

itens.explicacao: Since + ponto no tempo (my last birthday); for + duração (for two years).

itens.enunciado: 'Please ____ your phones before the test starts.'
itens.explicacao: Switch off / turn off = desligar.
porque: Certo: Switch off = desligar.
Plug in = ligar à tomada.
Switch over = mudar de canal ou de sistema, não desligar.
Switch up não significa desligar.

itens.enunciado: 'I can't hear the video. Can you ____?'
itens.explicacao: Verbo + it + partícula: turn it up.
porque: Certo: Aumentar o volume = turn up; com pronome fica no meio: turn it up.
Turn down = baixar o volume.
Turn off = desligar.
O pronome vai entre o verbo e a partícula.

itens.enunciado: 'Back up your files' means 'make a copy of your files so you don't lose them'.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. Back up = fazer uma cópia de segurança.

itens.enunciado: Complete with ONE word: 'It took me an hour to set ____ my new printer.'
itens.modelo: up
itens.explicacao: Set up = instalar e configurar um aparelho.

itens.enunciado: Complete with ONE word: 'Don't forget to log ____ when you use a school computer.'
itens.modelo: out
itens.explicacao: Log out (ou log off) = terminar a sessão.

licao.resumo: Os Media e a Comunicação Global (AE 10.º, B1): vocabulário dos media, passiva no presente e no passado, comparativos e superlativos e leitura sobre notícias falsas.
pontos: Media vocabulary: Vocabulário dos media: headline (título da notícia), article, journalist, reliable source (fonte fiável), fake news (notícias falsas), follower, influencer, post (publicação), broadcast (transmitir), viewer (espetador) e privacy (privacidade).
Passive: present and past: A passiva forma-se com be + particípio passado e usa-se quando importa mais a ação do que quem a faz.
Comparatives and superlatives: Adjetivos curtos: -er/-est (fast, faster, the fastest).
Reading: fake news: Em textos de opinião e informação, distingue factos (que se podem verificar) de opiniões (o que o autor pensa).
licao.exemplo: Before you share a post, check the headline and look for a reliable source.

itens.enunciado: The title of a newspaper article, in big letters, is the ____.
itens.explicacao: Headline é o título em destaque.
porque: deadline = prazo.
Certo: headline = título principal da notícia.
caption = legenda de uma fotografia.
subtitle = legenda de um filme ou subtítulo.

itens.enunciado: A video that is shared by millions of people very quickly goes ____.
itens.explicacao: Go viral é a expressão fixa.
porque: visual = relacionado com a vista.
Certo: Go viral = espalhar-se muito depressa na internet.
virtual = que existe só em formato digital.
vital = essencial.

itens.enunciado: A 'reliable source' is a source of information that you can trust.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. Reliable = fiável, em que se pode confiar.

itens.enunciado: Complete with ONE word: 'False stories that look like real news are called ____ news.'
itens.modelo: fake
itens.explicacao: Fake news = notícias falsas apresentadas como verdadeiras.

itens.enunciado: Write the noun for the person: 'journalism' → 'a ____'
itens.modelo: journalist
itens.explicacao: Journalism (a atividade) → journalist (a pessoa).

itens.enunciado: 'Hundreds of photos ____ on social media every second.'
itens.explicacao: Passiva = be + particípio passado.
porque: Certo: Sujeito plural + passiva no presente: are + particípio.
Na ativa, as fotos não publicam nada.
Is não concorda com photos (plural).
Are posting é ativa: as fotos não fazem a ação.

itens.enunciado: 'The first text message ____ in 1992.'
itens.explicacao: Passiva no passado = was/were + particípio.
porque: Certo: Passado + singular: was + particípio.
Is sent é presente; 1992 é passado.
Were não concorda com 'message' (singular).
Na ativa, a mensagem não enviou nada.

itens.enunciado: 'The video was made by two students' and 'Two students made the video' have the same meaning.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. Uma é passiva e a outra ativa; o sentido é o mesmo, muda o foco.

itens.enunciado: Rewrite in the passive: 'A famous journalist wrote the article.' → The article…
itens.modelo: The article was written by a famous journalist.
itens.explicacao: Wrote → was written; o sujeito da ativa passa a agente com by.

itens.enunciado: Complete with the passive form of the verb in brackets: 'English ____ (speak) in many countries.'
itens.modelo: is spoken
itens.explicacao: Present simple passivo: is + spoken (particípio de speak).

itens.enunciado: Rewrite in the passive, without the agent: 'Somebody stole my password.' → My password…
itens.modelo: My password was stolen.
itens.explicacao: Quando o agente é desconhecido (somebody), omite-se: was stolen.

itens.enunciado: 'Online news is ____ than printed newspapers.'
itens.explicacao: Adjetivo curto + -er + than.
porque: The não se usa antes do comparativo com than.
Fastest é superlativo e pediria the.
Certo: Fast é curto: faster than.
Com adjetivos curtos não se usa more.

itens.enunciado: 'For me, this is ____ app of all.'
itens.explicacao: Superlativo de adjetivo longo: the most + adjetivo.
porque: Certo: Useful é longo: the most useful.
The more compara duas coisas, não 'of all'.
Falta o artigo the no superlativo.
Adjetivos longos não levam -est.

itens.enunciado: 'This video is more good than the first one' is correct.
itens.explicacao: Falso. Good é irregular: better than.

itens.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the adjective in brackets: 'That was the ____ (bad) interview I have ever seen.'
itens.modelo: worst
itens.explicacao: Bad – worse – the worst.

itens.enunciado: Complete with ONE word: 'Tablets are usually cheaper ____ laptops.'
itens.modelo: than
itens.explicacao: Depois do comparativo usa-se than: cheaper than.

itens.enunciado: 'However' introduces an idea that contrasts with the previous one.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. However = no entanto; introduz um contraste.

itens.enunciado: Which sentence is an OPINION, not a fact?
opcoes: The video has over a thousand views on the school website.
Newspapers are more boring than social media.
itens.explicacao: Factos verificam-se; opiniões exprimem juízos.
porque: O número de visualizações pode verificar-se.
Uma data de fundação pode verificar-se.
O número de parágrafos pode contar-se.
Certo: 'More boring' é uma apreciação pessoal, não se pode verificar.

itens.enunciado: Read the text and answer the questions.
itens.excerto: Last spring, a short video showed a shark swimming in a flooded street. In a few hours it had thousands of shares. The only problem was that it was not real: someone had put an old photo of a shark into a picture of a city after a storm. Stories like this are called fake news, and they spread fast because they are surprising or make us angry. So how can we protect ourselves? First, look at the source. Is it a well-known newspaper or an account you have never heard of? Second, read more than the headline; headlines are written to catch your attention, not to tell the whole story. Third, search for the same story on other websites. If no reliable source mentions it, be careful. Finally, think before you share. Every time we share a false story, we help it travel further.

perguntas.enunciado: Why was the shark video fake?
opcoes: It was filmed during a real flood in a city.
It joined two different images into one.
The shark in the video was a robot.
Nobody shared it on social media.
perguntas.explicacao: someone had put an old photo of a shark into a picture of a city.
porque: O texto diz que não era real.
Certo: Alguém pôs uma foto antiga de um tubarão numa imagem de uma cidade.
O texto não fala de robô.
Teve milhares de partilhas.

perguntas.enunciado: According to the text, fake news spreads fast because it is surprising or makes people angry.
perguntas.explicacao: Verdadeiro. 'they spread fast because they are surprising or make us angry'.

perguntas.enunciado: Which word in the text means 'trustworthy'?
perguntas.modelo: reliable
perguntas.explicacao: 'If no reliable source mentions it'.

perguntas.enunciado: According to the writer, headlines…
opcoes: are written mainly to attract readers.
are the best way to check a story.
are always written by reliable sources only.
perguntas.explicacao: Catch your attention = atrair a atenção.
porque: O texto diz o contrário.
Certo: 'headlines are written to catch your attention, not to tell the whole story'.
O conselho é ler mais do que o título.
O texto não diz quem escreve os títulos.

itens.explicacao: Lê o texto com atenção e volta ao passo exato antes de responder.

itens.enunciado: Read the text and answer the questions.
itens.excerto: Inês is seventeen and has 40,000 followers. She posts videos about cheap vegetarian recipes, and companies sometimes send her products to try. 'People think it's easy money,' she says, 'but it's a lot of work. I film, edit and answer messages every day.' Inês has one rule: she always tells her followers when a company has paid her or given her something. 'If they can't trust me, they won't follow me,' she explains. Not all influencers are so honest. In many countries, the law says that paid posts must be clearly marked as advertising, but some influencers hide it. Inês thinks schools should teach young people how social media works. 'We spend hours online every day,' she says, 'but nobody teaches us to read it.'

perguntas.enunciado: What are Inês's videos about?
perguntas.explicacao: Recipes = receitas; cheap = baratas.
porque: Certo: 'She posts videos about cheap vegetarian recipes'.
As empresas enviam produtos, mas os vídeos são de receitas.
Ela não ensina a ser influencer.
O texto fala de receitas baratas.

perguntas.enunciado: Inês sometimes hides the fact that a company has paid her.
perguntas.explicacao: Falso. A regra dela é dizer sempre quando uma empresa lhe pagou ou ofereceu algo.

perguntas.enunciado: What does 'it' refer to in 'nobody teaches us to read it'?
perguntas.modelo: social media
perguntas.explicacao: It retoma 'social media' da frase anterior sobre como as redes funcionam.

itens.explicacao: Lê o texto com atenção e volta ao passo exato antes de responder.

modulos.titulo: 10.º ano (B1) — Teens in a global world

licao.resumo: Os Jovens na Era Global (AE 10.º, B1): vocabulário da vida dos jovens, modais de conselho e obrigação, formas de futuro e leitura sobre jovens e telemóveis.
pontos: Youth and lifestyle words: Vocabulário da vida dos jovens: teenager (adolescente), peer pressure (pressão dos colegas), generation gap (diferença entre gerações), pocket money (semanada), part-time job (trabalho em part-time), screen time (tempo de ecrã), healthy lifestyle (estilo de vida saudável) e volunteer (voluntário).
Advice and obligation: Should = conselho (You should sleep more).
Future: will and going to: Will: previsões e opiniões sobre o futuro (I think robots will do many jobs) e decisões tomadas no momento (I'll help you).
Reading: teens and phones: Nas perguntas de verdadeiro/falso, sublinha no texto a frase que prova a tua resposta.
licao.exemplo: Peer pressure can make teenagers spend more screen time than they want.

itens.enunciado: The money that parents give their children every week is ____.
itens.explicacao: Pocket money vem dos pais; salary vem de um emprego.
porque: bill = conta a pagar.
Certo: pocket money = semanada ou mesada.
salary = salário de um trabalhador.
part-time job = trabalho a tempo parcial, não dinheiro dos pais.

itens.enunciado: When friends make you do something because 'everybody does it', this is ____.
itens.explicacao: Peers = pessoas da mesma idade ou grupo.
porque: Certo: peer pressure = pressão dos colegas.
good advice = um bom conselho, não uma pressão.
screen time = tempo passado em frente a ecrãs.
generation gap = diferença entre gerações.

itens.enunciado: A 'volunteer' is a person who works without being paid.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. Volunteer = voluntário, trabalha sem receber dinheiro.

itens.enunciado: Complete with ONE word: 'There is a big generation ____ between my grandparents and me: we like completely different things.'
itens.modelo: gap
itens.explicacao: Generation gap = diferença de ideias e gostos entre gerações.

itens.enunciado: 'Screen time' means the time you spend at the cinema.
itens.explicacao: Falso. Screen time = tempo passado a olhar para ecrãs (telemóvel, computador, televisão).

itens.enunciado: 'You look tired. You ____ go to bed earlier.'
itens.explicacao: Should + infinitivo sem to = conselho.
porque: Can't exprime impossibilidade.
Mustn't proíbe; aqui aconselha-se o contrário.
Certo: Dar um conselho: should.
Don't have to diz que não é preciso; não é conselho.

itens.enunciado: 'It's Saturday tomorrow, so we ____ get up early.'
itens.explicacao: Don't have to = não é preciso; mustn't = é proibido.
porque: Not allowed to = proibição, como mustn't.
Mustn't seria proibição de acordar cedo.
Certo: Não é necessário: don't have to.
Have to diz que é obrigatório, o contrário do sentido.

itens.enunciado: 'You mustn't smoke here' means smoking is not allowed.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. Mustn't exprime proibição.

itens.enunciado: Complete with ONE word: 'Students ____ wear a helmet when they ride a bike to school. It's the rule.' (obligation)
itens.modelo: must
itens.explicacao: Uma regra exprime-se com must (ou have to).

itens.enunciado: Correct the mistake: 'You should to talk to your parents about it.' →
itens.modelo: You should talk to your parents about it.
itens.explicacao: Depois de should vem o infinitivo sem to.

itens.enunciado: 'You don't have to come' and 'You mustn't come' mean the same.
itens.explicacao: Falso. Don't have to = não é necessário; mustn't = é proibido.

itens.enunciado: 'Look at those black clouds! It ____ rain.'
itens.explicacao: Prova visível agora → be going to.
porque: Will serve para previsões sem prova visível.
O present simple não exprime previsão.
Esta forma não existe.
Certo: Previsão com prova no presente (as nuvens): be going to.

itens.enunciado: 'The phone is ringing.' – 'Don't worry, I ____ answer it.'
itens.explicacao: Decisão espontânea → will.
porque: O present simple não exprime decisão no momento.
Going to é para planos já decididos.
Certo: Decisão tomada no momento: will ('ll).
Esta forma não existe.

itens.enunciado: 'I'm meeting my friends at the cinema at 8' talks about a fixed arrangement in the future.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. O present continuous exprime combinações já marcadas.

itens.enunciado: Complete with the going to form of the verb in brackets: 'Next year my sister ____ (study) in Spain with Erasmus.'
itens.modelo: is going to study
itens.explicacao: Plano já decidido: is going to study.

itens.enunciado: Complete with will and the verb in brackets: 'I think people ____ (not/use) cash in twenty years.'
itens.modelo: won't use
itens.explicacao: Previsão/opinião (I think) → will; negativa: won't use.

itens.enunciado: In a reading test, you should answer using your general knowledge, not the text.
itens.explicacao: Falso. A resposta tem de estar justificada no texto, não no que sabes ou achas.

itens.enunciado: In a reading test, if the text says 'some teenagers' and the statement says 'all teenagers', the statement is usually false.
itens.explicacao: Verdadeiro. Some e all não têm o mesmo sentido.

itens.enunciado: Read the text and answer the questions.
itens.excerto: Last September, a secondary school near Porto decided to ban mobile phones during breaks. Students now leave their phones in a box at the entrance and get them back at the end of the day. At first, many of them were angry. 'I felt naked without my phone,' says Rita, 15. But after a few weeks, something changed. Teachers noticed that students were talking and playing more in the playground. The library, which was usually empty at lunchtime, became busy. Even Rita admits that she is happier. 'I used to check my phone every five minutes. Now I actually talk to my friends.' Not everyone agrees, though. Some parents say they need to contact their children during the day, and the school has a phone in the office for emergencies. The headteacher thinks the rule will stay. 'We aren't against technology,' she says. 'We just want our students to look up from their screens.'

perguntas.enunciado: How did many students feel when the rule started?
opcoes: They wanted to bring more phones.
perguntas.explicacao: Angry = zangados: não gostaram da regra.
porque: O texto diz que estavam zangados.
Rita diz que se sentia 'naked', por isso notaram muito.
Certo: 'At first, many of them were angry.'
Nada disto aparece no texto.

perguntas.enunciado: After the ban, the school library became more popular at lunchtime.
perguntas.explicacao: Verdadeiro. 'The library, which was usually empty at lunchtime, became busy.'

perguntas.enunciado: Which word in the text means 'prohibit'?
perguntas.modelo: ban
perguntas.explicacao: 'decided to ban mobile phones during breaks'.

perguntas.enunciado: What does the headteacher mean by 'look up from their screens'?
opcoes: stop using technology completely, even at home
read more books in the library
perguntas.explicacao: A expressão é figurada: dar atenção ao mundo real.
porque: Ela diz 'We aren't against technology'.
Não tem nada a ver com tamanho de ecrãs.
A biblioteca é um exemplo, não o sentido da frase.
Certo: 'Look up' = levantar os olhos do ecrã e ver o que está à volta.

itens.explicacao: Lê o texto com atenção e volta ao passo exato antes de responder.

itens.enunciado: Read the text and answer the questions.
itens.excerto: Many teenagers say that the hardest question adults ask them is 'What do you want to do in the future?' Duarte, 17, is one of them. 'My grandfather worked in the same factory for forty years,' he says. 'I don't think that will happen to me.' Like many young people, Duarte expects to change jobs several times and maybe live in another country. He is going to study computer science, but he also wants to learn Spanish and German. 'Languages are like a passport,' he explains. His friend Leonor has a different plan. She wants to take a gap year after secondary school and work as a volunteer in an animal shelter. Her parents were worried at first, but now they support her. 'You don't have to know everything at seventeen,' her mother says. 'You have to be curious and ready to learn.'

perguntas.enunciado: What does Duarte think about his future?
opcoes: He will never leave his home town.
He will probably have several different jobs.
He doesn't want to go to university.
He will work in his grandfather's factory for forty years.
perguntas.explicacao: Expects to change jobs several times.
porque: Ele pensa que talvez viva noutro país.
Certo: 'Duarte expects to change jobs several times'.
Ele vai estudar informática.
Ele diz que isso não lhe vai acontecer.

perguntas.enunciado: Leonor's parents have always supported her plan for a gap year.
perguntas.explicacao: Falso. 'Her parents were worried at first, but now they support her.'

perguntas.enunciado: Duarte says 'Languages are like a passport'. Explain what he means in one sentence (8–20 words).
perguntas.modelo: He means that languages open doors and help you travel, work and live in other countries.
perguntas.explicacao: Um passaporte permite entrar noutros países: as línguas também dão acesso a oportunidades lá fora.

itens.explicacao: Lê o texto com atenção e volta ao passo exato antes de responder.

licao.resumo: Passatempos e relações pessoais (temas do 10.º e do exame 550): vocabulário de tempos livres e amizade, first e second conditional e orações relativas restritivas.
pontos: Hobbies and relationships: Expressões frequentes: take up a hobby (começar um passatempo), join a club (entrar num clube), hang out with friends (passar tempo com amigos), get on well with (dar-se bem com), fall out with (zangar-se com), make friends (fazer amigos).
First conditional: O first conditional fala de situações reais ou prováveis no futuro: If + present simple, will + infinitivo (If it rains, we will stay at home).

Second conditional: O second conditional fala de situações imaginárias ou pouco prováveis no presente ou no futuro: If + past simple, would + infinitivo (If I had more time, I would learn the guitar).
Defining relative clauses: As orações relativas restritivas dizem de que pessoa ou coisa falamos.
licao.exemplo: I joined a book club last year and made friends with people I get on really well with.

itens.enunciado: 'I get ____ well with my sister; we never argue.'
itens.explicacao: Get on (well) with someone.
porque: Get in = entrar.
Get off = sair de um transporte.
Get up = levantar-se.
Certo: Get on well with = dar-se bem com.

itens.enunciado: 'It's easy to ____ friends when you join a sports team.'
itens.explicacao: Make friends é uma colocação fixa.
porque: Take não forma esta expressão.
Do friends não existe em inglês.
Certo: Make friends = fazer amigos.
Have friends = ter amigos, não fazer novos.

itens.enunciado: 'Ana fell out with her best friend' means they started a new friendship.
itens.explicacao: Falso. Fall out with = zangar-se, deixar de se dar bem.

itens.enunciado: Complete with ONE word: 'I've decided to take ____ photography as a new hobby.'
itens.modelo: up
itens.explicacao: Take up a hobby = começar um passatempo.

itens.enunciado: Complete with ONE word: 'On Fridays I usually hang ____ with my friends in the park.'
itens.modelo: out
itens.explicacao: Hang out (with) = passar tempo juntos, sem plano especial.

itens.enunciado: 'If you ____ the club, you'll meet people with the same interests.'
itens.explicacao: If + present, will + infinitivo.
porque: Joined pertence ao second conditional.
Will não vai na oração com if.
Would pertence ao second conditional.
Certo: Na oração com if usa-se o present simple.

itens.enunciado: '____ you leave now, you'll miss the start of the match.'
itens.explicacao: Unless = if … not.
porque: Provided (that) = desde que; daria o sentido contrário.
When indica tempo e mudaria o sentido.
Certo: Unless = if not: se não saíres agora, perdes o início.
Com if, o sentido seria o contrário (se saíres, perdes).

itens.enunciado: 'If it will rain tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic' is correct.
itens.explicacao: Falso. Na oração com if usa-se o present: If it rains tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.

itens.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets: 'If we win this game, we ____ (play) in the final.'
itens.modelo: will play
itens.explicacao: Oração principal do first conditional: will + infinitivo.

itens.enunciado: Make a first conditional sentence with these words: you / study / for the test → pass
itens.modelo: If you study for the test, you will pass.
itens.explicacao: If + present simple, will + infinitivo.

itens.enunciado: 'If I ____ a lot of money, I would travel around the world.'
itens.explicacao: If + past simple, would + infinitivo.
porque: Certo: Situação imaginária: if + past simple.
Will pertence ao first conditional.
Would não vai na oração com if.
Have é first conditional (situação real).

itens.enunciado: 'If I were you, I ____ to the teacher about the problem.'
itens.explicacao: If I were you, I would… = conselho.
porque: Will não combina com o past (were) da condição.
Depois de would vem o infinitivo, não o particípio.
Talked iria para a oração com if, não para a principal.
Certo: Conselho com If I were you: would + infinitivo.
